about: The stand's published numbers (benchmarks/tasks/README.md): each one as the script printed it, keyed step:field, and each passage of the docs that quotes them, with {step:field|format} where a number stands. stand.py check compares the docs with these numbers and, with --measured, these numbers with a run. Change a number here and in the doc together, from a run.
measured_with: solvi 0.8.0 (published); reproduced with 0.9.0.dev0 from the packed replies

The guard did not solve more tasks ({taubench/solution:solved} against {taubench/baseline:solved}; one run, a simulated customer — a few tasks are noise). It stopped every call the environment would have refused before it was made, and recorded {taubench/solution:guard.decisions} decisions that all replay.

Every quote is literally in the contract ({cuad/solution:quotes_verbatim} of {cuad/solution:quotes_verbatim/of}; the baseline's {cuad/baseline:quotes_verbatim} of {cuad/baseline:quotes_verbatim/of}), fewer false claims, and `System.guarantee` on a trust score answers two thirds alone at {cuad/solution:wrong_among_answered_alone|.1%} wrong, where the baseline cannot say "not sure". It finds fewer clauses ({cuad/solution:found_of_present} against {cuad/baseline:found_of_present}).

The judge inside solvi is not better than the plain call (F1 {ragtruth/solution:all.f1} against {ragtruth/baseline:all.f1}). Under a 10% risk promise only {ragtruth/solution:answered_alone.all.share|.0%} is answered alone, with {ragtruth/solution:answered_alone_and_wrong|.1%} of all responses answered alone and wrong

A plain threshold (the baseline, or solvi's `System.guarantee` without new intents: {banking77/solution_plain:after.answered_alone|.1%} answered, {banking77/solution_plain:after.error_among_answered|.1%} wrong after the shift) breaks the promise; `OpenSetGate` keeps it and flags the shift {banking77/solution:flagged_after_shift} requests after it starts

solvi does not write better queries ({bird/solution:solution.right} against {bird/baseline:right} right). It decides which ones can go out alone: wrong among those {bird/solution:solution.wrong_among_answered|.1%} instead of {bird/baseline:wrong_among_answered|.1%}. Answering only when all three sampled queries return the same rows: {bird/solution:unanimous.answered|.1%} answered, {bird/solution:unanimous.wrong_among_answered|.1%} wrong (same script).

give {abtbuy/solution:head + one counterpart.f1}. It is supervised ({abtbuy/solution:dev_pairs_fitted|,} labelled pairs), the baseline is zero-shot.
